storylines.label: Jev TypeSafe
storylines.latest_title: [AINews] TypeSafe/Jev at >$100M ARR, $7.5B valuation 3 weeks after launch

prior_narrative.tldr: TypeSafe AI launched Jev as a decision-only "System One" model that classifies, routes, and scores, claiming over 100x the speed and 200x the cost efficiency of small frontier LLMs. LangChain published an integration guide and InfoQ described its typed-probability output.
prior_narrative.whats_new: AINews reported Oct 10 that TypeSafe/Jev passed $100M ARR at a $7.5B valuation three weeks after launch; the figures are the newsletter's headline claim, not an audited disclosure.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A purpose-built model that's 100x faster and 200x cheaper than a small frontier LLM is a strong fit for the classify/route/score steps buried inside most agent pipelines — the exact spots teams currently overpay a general-purpose LLM to handle.

beats.headline: LangChain documents Jev's place in the agent loop
beats.summary: A first-party guide to TypeSafe AI's "System One" model moves Jev from announcement to wiring instructions.

beats.headline: InfoQ: Jev returns typed probabilities, not text
beats.summary: Output is a structured decision with typed probabilities, which is what makes it droppable into classify/route/score steps.

beats.headline: Reported >$100M ARR and $7.5B valuation three weeks after launch
beats.summary: Commercial traction is claimed in a newsletter headline; the underlying figures are not yet independently sourced here.

open_questions: Do Jev's speed/cost claims hold up against a real agent pipeline's classify/route/score calls, not just TypeSafe's own benchmarks?
Will other labs ship a comparable decision-model category, or does this stay a single-vendor niche?
Do typed probabilities from Jev stay calibrated on a team's own routing labels, not just TypeSafe's evaluation sets?
Do TypeSafe or an independent source confirm the >$100M ARR and $7.5B valuation figures?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If a general-purpose LLM call in your agent pipeline only classifies, routes, or scores, benchmark Jev against it on your own labels; treat the ARR and valuation reports as adoption signal, not performance evidence.

prior_narrative.tldr: On Oct 1, Anthropic's Claude Code team published a guide to mods: hooks that ship inside plugins and run within a Claude Code session. The guide builds one from an empty folder, then tours two larger mods.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Digitimes (Oct 5) frames DeepSeek Harness's Claude Code mods bridge and open plugin architecture as a challenge to agent lock-in, following the Oct 4 v0.2.1-alpha.1 compatibility layer.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Mods are a plugin-level extension point, so a second agent runtime accepting the same format lowers the cost of moving mod-based workflows between harnesses.

status.detail: Claude Code mods have an official guide, an experimental DeepSeek Harness compatibility layer, and now trade-press framing as an anti-lock-in move.

beats.headline: Claude Code mods guide: hooks shipped inside plugins
beats.summary: Walks through building a mod from an empty folder and two larger examples.

beats.headline: DeepSeek Harness adds an experimental mods compatibility layer
beats.summary: Alpha release, DeepSeek rejecting the "copying homework" charge, and a Digitimes read of it as an open-plugin challenge to lock-in.

open_questions: Does the Harness compatibility layer run existing Claude Code mods unmodified, or only a subset of hooks?
Will Anthropic document mods as a stable cross-runtime format, or keep them Claude Code specific?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you build Claude Code mods, keep hook logic free of Claude-specific paths for now; test against the Harness alpha only on throwaway projects until its coverage is documented.

prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic added build-eval and hillclimb commands to its claude-api plugin on Sep 28, alongside a post on designing evals without fooling yourself. Hamel Husain reviewed the tooling two days later.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Hamel Husain reviewed the new build_eval and hill-climb commands on Sep 30, calling a first-party Anthropic eval tool likely to shape how teams build evals.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A first-party eval workflow in the Claude Code plugin sets a default for how many teams will build graders and iterate prompts, so its grader checks and overfitting guardrails are worth auditing before you adopt them.

beats.headline: Anthropic adds build-eval and hillclimb commands to the claude-api plugin
beats.summary: The post pairs the commands with principles for hillclimbing against evals without overfitting to them.

beats.headline: Hamel Husain reviews the tool: build evals, check graders, improve against them
beats.summary: He normally skips eval-tool reviews because they age fast, but expects a first-party tool to influence practice.

open_questions: Does the grader check in build_eval catch graders that score the wrong behavior, in independent use?
Do hillclimb gains hold up on held-out cases rather than the eval set it optimized against?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Run build_eval on one existing agent task and compare its graders against your hand-written ones before replacing them; hold out a case set that hillclimb never sees.

storylines.label: OpenAI DevDay
storylines.latest_title: [AINews] OpenAI DevDay 2026: Dots, 6.1 Sol, Ultrafast, Decisions API, Agents API, Spaces, Marketplace, and 1.2 Billion ChatGPT WAU

prior_narrative.tldr: OpenAI used its Sep 29 DevDay to announce GPT-6.1 Sol, computer use in the Agents API, cloud-based Codex environments, a Decisions API and new ChatGPT plugin capabilities. Simon Willison live-blogged the keynote from the floor.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Latent Space's Sep 30 recap lists the full slate (Dots, 6.1 Sol, Ultrafast, Decisions API, Agents API, Spaces, Marketplace) and cites 1.2 billion ChatGPT weekly users.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Computer use in the Agents API and hosted Codex environments move more agent execution onto OpenAI's platform, which changes where you run, sandbox and bill agent workloads.

status.detail: DevDay products were announced Sep 29; the coverage here does not give GA dates, pricing or limits.

beats.headline: DevDay 2026: GPT-6.1 Sol, Agents API computer use, cloud Codex, Decisions API
beats.summary: InfoQ's developer recap and Simon Willison's live blog cover the keynote day.

beats.headline: Latent Space tallies the full slate, from Spaces and Marketplace to 1.2B ChatGPT WAU

open_questions: What pricing and rate limits apply to computer use in the Agents API?
When do cloud-based Codex environments and the Decisions API reach general availability?
How does GPT-6.1 Sol perform in independent evals against the prior GPT-6 Astra?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Do not migrate agent workloads to the new Agents API or hosted Codex yet: run your own evals on GPT-6.1 Sol and wait for published pricing and limits before changing sandboxing or cost budgets.
